mainTopic: כיסוי הדם: who must cover, when the duty returns, the slaughterer's right to the מצוה, and blood mixed with other liquids
overview: The amud opens by rejecting a comparison to the story of רב's students: drinking and saying a ברכה can't happen together, but slaughtering and covering can. A new משנה then teaches about כיסוי הדם. Anyone who sees uncovered blood must cover it. Blood that a person covered does not need covering again if it becomes uncovered. Blood the wind covered is different. Three ברייתות on "וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה" teach that everyone shares this duty, that the blood is covered by hand and not with the foot, and that the מצוה belongs to the slaughterer. רבן גמליאל fined someone ten gold coins for grabbing it. The גמרא asks whether that payment is for the מצוה or for the ברכה, and a story about רבי and a guest shows it is ten coins per ברכה, so forty for ברכת המזון. Next, the word וכסהו explains why covering is done only once, unlike returning a lost item. רבי יוחנן limits the wind case to blood that became uncovered again, which teaches אין דיחוי אצל מצות. Finally, a new משנה begins on blood mixed with water, wine, or the blood of a בהמה, and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rejecting the comparison to the story of רב's students
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away an earlier comparison. Drinking and saying a ברכה can't happen at the same time, but slaughtering and covering can.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare these? There, you can't drink and say a ברכה at the same time. Here, you can slaughter with one hand and cover with the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects a proof brought just before this, which compared our case to the story of רב's students. It explains why the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב's students, asking for a cup for the ברכה showed they had stopped drinking, because the two acts can't overlap. Covering the blood of one animal and slaughtering the next can be done at the same moment, one with each hand. So covering in between is not a real break in the slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: "How can you compare?!" A phrase used to reject a comparison.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, drinking and saying a blessing
phrases.notes: "There" means the story of רב's students, which the גמרא used just before as a comparison.

phrases.english: at the same time is not possible;
here, it is possible to slaughter with one hand
and cover with the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison brought just before this section
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof taken from the story of רב's students
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Drinking and a ברכה can't overlap, but slaughtering and covering can, so the cases are not alike
steps.whatToRemember: Covering one animal's blood before slaughtering the next is not a break, because both acts could be done at the same time.

steps.title: משנה: when someone else must cover, and when covering is not needed again
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three rules. Someone who sees uncovered blood must cover it. Blood that was covered and then uncovered is exempt. Blood covered by the wind still has to be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughtered and didn't cover, and another person saw it, that person must cover. If he covered it and it became uncovered, he is exempt from covering again. If the wind covered it, he is obligated to cover.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with three short cases about כיסוי הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duty to cover is not only on the slaughterer, so anyone who sees the blood must do it. Once the blood was covered properly, the מצוה is done, and it does not come back if the blood is uncovered later. When the wind covered the blood, no person did the covering, so the duty stays.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to cover the blood of a wild animal or bird after slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the second and third cases. If a person covered the blood, the מצוה is finished even if it gets uncovered. If the wind covered it, the מצוה was never done, so the duty comes back. Step 16 explains that this applies once the blood becomes uncovered again.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one slaughtered and did not cover,
and another person saw it, he is obligated to cover.
If he covered it and it became uncovered,
he is exempt from covering it again.
If the wind covered it,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording, which makes the wind the one that covered it.

phrases.english: he is obligated to cover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who sees uncovered blood must cover it. Blood that a person covered is exempt even if it later becomes uncovered. Covering by the wind does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the מצוה is tied to the blood being covered by a person, not only to the slaughterer.

steps.title: ברייתא: the slaughterer covers, and anyone who sees must also cover
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה" that the slaughterer covers. It learns from "וָאֹמַר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" that anyone else who sees the blood must cover it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "And he shall pour out and cover" means the one who poured out the blood should cover it. If he slaughtered and did not cover, and someone else saw it, how do we know that person must cover? Because it says "And I said to the children of Israel", which is a warning to all of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק source for the משנה's first case, that someone else who sees the blood must cover it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה" by itself would suggest only the slaughterer is obligated. The words "לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" widen the command to every Jew. So when the slaughterer fails to cover, anyone who sees the blood takes on the duty.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall pour out and cover" (ויקרא 17:13)
A warning or command from the תורה
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And he shall pour out and cover":
the one who poured out the blood shall cover it.
If one slaughtered and did not cover, and another person saw it,
from where do we know that he is obligated to cover?
As it says: "And I said to the children of Israel":
this is a warning to all the children of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה מִי שֶׁשָּׁפַךְ יְכַסֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's first case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The slaughterer covers, and if he doesn't, any Jew who sees the blood must cover it.

steps.title: ברייתא: cover with the hand, not with the foot
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from "וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה" that you cover with the same thing you poured with, meaning the hand, so מצוות won't be treated with disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא: "And he shall pour out and cover" means that with what he poured out the blood, with that he should cover it. He should not cover it with his foot, so that מצוות will not be disgraceful to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא on the same פסוק. This one teaches how the covering must be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words of the פסוק are read as a pair: the tool used for pouring, the hand holding the knife, is also the tool for covering. Kicking dirt with the foot would treat a מצוה with contempt.

keyTerms.meaning: מצוות treated as disgraceful or cheap

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"And he shall pour out and cover":
with what he poured out, with that he shall cover,
phrases.notes: He poured out the blood with his hand, holding the knife, so he should cover with his hand.

phrases.english: that he should not cover it with his foot,
so that מצוות will not be disgraceful to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה בַּמֶּה שֶׁשָּׁפַךְ בּוֹ יְכַסֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק, this time about how to cover
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood must be covered by hand, not with the foot, out of respect for מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a well-known source for the idea that one must not treat a מצוה with disrespect.

steps.title: ברייתא: the one who poured is the one who covers
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא learns from "וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה" that the slaughterer himself is the one who should cover. The מצוה is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא: "And he shall pour out and cover" means the one who poured out the blood is the one who should cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא on the פסוק. It stresses that the slaughterer has first right to the מצוה of covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הוּא ("he") puts the weight on the slaughterer himself. The מצוה belongs to him, so someone else should not take it away from him. The next step shows what happens when someone does.
steps.confusionAlert: This sounds the same as the first ברייתא, but the point is different. The first one teaches that others must cover when the slaughterer didn't. This one teaches that the slaughterer has the right to the מצוה, so nobody should grab it from him.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"And he shall pour out and cover":
the one who poured out the blood is the one who shall cover it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה מִי שֶׁשָּׁפַךְ הוּא יְכַסֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, stressing the slaughterer's right
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of covering belongs to the slaughterer.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל fines a man who grabbed someone else's מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A story: someone covered another person's slaughter before the slaughterer could. רבן גמליאל made him pay the slaughterer ten gold coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case of a man who slaughtered, and his friend jumped ahead and covered the blood. רבן גמליאל obligated the friend to give him ten gold coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up its rule with a real case. Taking someone else's מצוה cost the grabber money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the מצוה of covering belongs to the slaughterer, the friend took something that was his. רבן גמליאל treated this like a real loss and set a payment of ten gold coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Went ahead first, beat him to it

steps.whatToRemember: The slaughterer has the right to the מצוה of covering. Someone who grabs it from him must pay ten gold coins, as רבן גמליאל ruled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is the source for the idea that taking away someone else's מצוה is a real loss that can carry a payment.

phrases.english: There was an incident with one who slaughtered,
and his friend went ahead of him and covered the blood,
and Rabban Gamliel obligated him
to give him ten gold coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case that supports the third ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the מצוה of covering belongs to the slaughterer
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבן גמליאל, who made the grabber pay ten gold coins

steps.title: What do the ten gold coins pay for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבן גמליאל's ten-coin penalty pays for the stolen מצוה or for the stolen ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: is the payment for the מצוה, or for the ברכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ten gold coins from the רבן גמליאל story. It asks what exactly the person who covered the blood was paying for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who covered the blood took two things from the slaughterer: the מצוה of covering, and the ברכה said on it. The גמרא wants to know which one the ten coins are for.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised; it opens a real question that the גמרא then tries to resolve
Payment for the lost מצוה itself
Payment for the lost ברכה said over the מצוה

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is it payment for the מצוה, or payment for the blessing?
phrases.notes: "It" means the ten gold coins רבן גמליאל made him pay in the last story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the penalty in the רבן גמליאל story was actually for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ten coins pay for the מצוה or for the ברכה.

steps.title: The practical difference: ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the question matters. ברכת המזון is one מצוה but has four ברכות, so the payment would be either ten coins or forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? For ברכת המזון. If the payment is for the מצוה, there is one. If it is for the ברכה, there are four, which makes forty coins. So which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question matters in practice, and then asks again which answer is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In כיסוי הדם there is one מצוה and one ברכה, so both views give ten coins. With ברכת המזון the two views split. Counting by מצוה gives one payment of ten, and counting by ברכה gives four payments, forty coins.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
The blessings said after a meal
What is the answer? It brings the question back for a ruling

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For Grace after Meals.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ שְׂכַר מִצְוָה – אַחַת הִיא,
phrases.english: If you say it is payment for the מצוה, it is one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ שְׂכַר בְּרָכָה – הָוְיָין אַרְבָּעִים.
phrases.english: and if you say payment for the blessing, it comes to forty.
phrases.notes: ברכת המזון has four ברכות, and four times ten coins is forty.

phrases.english: So what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the real-life result of the question asked in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two views give different results.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ברכת המזון: ten coins if we count the מצוה, forty if we count the ברכות.

steps.title: A מין argues with רבי about two creators
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a story as its proof. A מין claims a פסוק shows that two different gods made the mountains and the wind. רבי answers from the end of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a מין told רבי that whoever made the mountains did not make the wind, and whoever made the wind did not make the mountains, because the פסוק says "He forms mountains and creates wind." רבי answered: "Fool, look at the end of the פסוק: 'ה׳ צבאות is His name.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that will answer the question. This first part only sets the scene, so stay with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מין reads two different verbs, forming and creating, as two different creators. רבי shows that the same פסוק ends with one Name, so a single God does both. The proof itself comes later in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who denies the תורה's beliefs

steps.confusionAlert: This argument about creation is not the proof. It only sets up the story. The proof comes at the meal at the end.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For a certain heretic said to Rebbi:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיָּצַר הָרִים לֹא בָּרָא רוּחַ,
phrases.english: The one who formed mountains did not create wind,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי שֶׁבָּרָא רוּחַ לֹא יָצַר הָרִים,
phrases.english: and the one who created wind did not form mountains,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי הִנֵּה יוֹצֵר הָרִים וּבֹרֵא רוּחַ״.
phrases.english: as it is written: "For behold, He forms mountains and creates wind."
He said to him: Fool,
go down to the end of the verse:
"The Lord of Hosts is His name."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the story the גמרא brings to answer the question in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the penalty is counted per ברכה or per מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי and the מין (opening scene).

steps.title: Three days of fasting, and a מין at the door
steps.stepSummary: The מין asks for three days to come back with an answer. רבי fasts for those three days. When he is about to eat, he hears a מין is at the door and quotes a sad פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מין said: "Give me three days and I will come back with an answer." רבי sat in fasts for three days. When he was about to eat, they told him, "A מין is at the door." He said: "They put bitterness into my meal."
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going and leads up to the meal where the proof will come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי fasted while the מין looked for an answer. Just as he finally sat down to eat, the news of a מין at the door felt like it was spoiling his meal. The story is moving toward the meal, where the ברכת המזון question will come up.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong answer that knocks down someone's argument

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְקוֹט לִי זִימְנָא תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: Give me a time of three days,
and I will come back to you with a refutation.
Rebbi sat three fasts.
When he was about to have his meal,
they said to him: A heretic is standing at the door.
He said: "They put bitterness into my food, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים סט:כב. The word בברותי ("my food") fits nicely with מיברא, the meal he was about to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story toward the meal.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the penalty is counted per ברכה or per מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי and the מין (middle scene).

steps.title: Good news and a meal invitation
steps.stepSummary: The person at the door brings good news: the first מין found no answer, fell from a roof, and died. רבי invites him to eat, and he agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: "רבי, I bring you good news. Your enemy found no answer, fell from the roof, and died." רבי asked: "Would you like to eat with me?" He said: "Yes."
steps.whatsHappening: The story sets up the meal. This is what makes the ברכת המזון question possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This visitor is not the first מין, since he reports that the first one died. Inviting him to eat creates the setting for ברכת המזון, which leads to the proof in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, מְבַשֵּׂר טוֹבוֹת אֲנִי לָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Rebbi, I bring you good news,
phrases.notes: This is a different man from the first מין. He is telling רבי what happened to the first one.

phrases.english: your enemy did not find an answer
and fell from the roof and died.
He said to him: Would you like to dine with me?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the story to the meal.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the penalty is counted per ברכה or per מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי and the מין (the meal invitation).

steps.title: The כוס של ברכה is worth forty gold coins
steps.stepSummary: After the meal, רבי offers the guest a choice: lead ברכת המזון over the cup, or take forty gold coins. The guest takes the cup, and a בת קול says the cup is worth forty gold coins. So each ברכה is worth ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they ate and drank, רבי asked: "Will you drink the כוס של ברכה, or take forty gold coins?" He said: "I will drink the כוס של ברכה." A בת קול came out and said: "The כוס של ברכה is worth forty gold coins."
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the proof. Leading ברכת המזון is valued at forty gold coins, not ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the payment were for the מצוה, ברכת המזון would be worth only ten coins, since it is one מצוה. Its value is forty, which is ten coins for each of the four ברכות. So the payment counts the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of wine held while leading ברכת המזון

steps.whatToRemember: The penalty is ten gold coins for each ברכה, not for each מצוה. Leading ברכת המזון, with its four ברכות, is worth forty gold coins.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much each single ברכה is worth, and that taking someone else's ברכה is a real loss to him.

phrases.english: After they ate and drank,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה אַתָּה שׁוֹתֶה
phrases.english: he said to him: Will you drink the cup of blessing,
or will you take forty gold coins?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה אֲנִי שׁוֹתֶה.
phrases.english: He said to him: I will drink the cup of blessing.
A Heavenly voice came out and said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה שָׁוֶה אַרְבָּעִים זְהוּבִים.
phrases.english: The cup of blessing is worth forty gold coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה אַתָּה שׁוֹתֶה אוֹ אַרְבָּעִים זְהוּבִים אַתָּה נוֹטֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and gives the actual proof for the question in steps 7 and 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the penalty is counted per ברכה (שכר ברכה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's offer of forty gold coins for ברכת המזון, which the בת קול confirmed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The payment is for the ברכה: ten gold coins for each ברכה, so forty for ברכת המזון.

steps.title: The guest's family still lives in Rome
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק adds a closing note to the story: the family of the guest who ate with רבי is still among the great families of Rome, called the family of בר לויאנוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: That family still exists among the important families of Rome, and it is called the family of בר לויאנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story about רבי and his guest with a short historical note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new הלכה. רבי יצחק simply identifies the guest's family, which was still known among the important families of Rome in his day.

keyTerms.meaning: The great, important families of Rome

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
That family still exists
phrases.notes: He means the family of the guest who ate with רבי.

phrases.english: among the great ones of Rome,
and they call it
the family of bar Luyyanus.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: עֲדַיִין יֶשְׁנָהּ לְאוֹתָהּ מִשְׁפָּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an ending to the story that was just told.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guest's family is still known in Rome as the family of בר לויאנוס.

steps.title: Why not cover again, like returning a lost item?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if blood was covered and then uncovered, you do not have to cover it again. רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי why this is different from השבת אבידה, which you must do even a hundred times.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he covered it and it became uncovered,' he does not need to cover it again. רב אחא בריה דרבא asked רב אשי: Why is this different from returning a lost item? There the Master said: 'Return' means even a hundred times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and challenges its rule by comparing it to השבת אבידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a lost item, if the animal runs away again, you must return it again, even a hundred times. So why should covering blood be done only once, even if the blood becomes uncovered again? The challenge is that two similar מצוות seem to follow different rules.

keyTerms.meaning: He covered it and it became uncovered
The מצוה of returning a lost item

phrases.english: "If he covered it and it became uncovered."
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה, which says that in this case he does not have to cover it again.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
What is different from returning a lost item,
where the Master said:
"Return" means even a hundred times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to analyzing the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that blood that was covered and then uncovered does not need to be covered again.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With השבת אבידה, the מצוה repeats each time the item is lost again. So covering blood should also repeat each time the blood is uncovered.

steps.title: The word 'cover it' limits the מצוה to once
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the פסוק about returning a lost item has no limiting word, but the פסוק about covering blood says 'וכסהו', which limits it to one time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, no limiting word is written. Here, a limiting word is written: 'and he shall cover it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by pointing to a difference in the wording of the two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the lost item does not limit how many times you must return it, so the מצוה repeats. The word וכסהו, 'cover it', is read as a מיעוט, a limiting word: cover it once and you are done.

keyTerms.meaning: A limiting word in the פסוק that narrows the law

steps.whatToRemember: Covering the blood is a one-time מצוה because the פסוק says וכסהו. Returning a lost item can repeat because its פסוק has no such limit.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, no limiting word is written;
here, a limiting word is written:
"and he shall cover it."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13. The word 'it' is read as one time only.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא כְּתִיב מִיעוּטָא, הָכָא כְּתִיב מִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from השבת אבידה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual distinction between the two פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering blood should repeat, like returning a lost item.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word וכסהו limits covering blood to a single time.

steps.title: Wind-covered blood: only if it was uncovered again
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the wind covered the blood, he must cover it. רבי יוחנן explains that this is only when the blood later became uncovered again. If it stayed covered, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If the wind covered it,' he must cover it. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this when it later became uncovered again. But if it did not become uncovered again, he is exempt from covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, and רבי יוחנן limits when that rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this explanation, you might think that when the wind covers the blood you must uncover it and cover it yourself. רבי יוחנן says no: the duty only comes back if the blood becomes exposed again.

phrases.english: "If the wind covered it."
phrases.notes: Again words from the משנה, which says he must cover it in this case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
They only taught this when it later became uncovered again;
but if it did not become uncovered again,
he is exempt from covering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood covered by the wind must be covered only if it later became uncovered again. Otherwise he is exempt.

steps.title: Wasn't the blood already pushed aside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: once the wind covered the blood, it was pushed out of the מצוה. Why should it come back when the blood is uncovered again?
steps.simpleTranslation: And when it became uncovered again, so what? It was already pushed aside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule with the idea of דיחוי, being pushed aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wind covered the blood, there was nothing left for the person to cover, so the מצוה could not be done. The challenge assumes that once a מצוה is pushed aside like this, it is gone for good, even if the blood is exposed later.

keyTerms.meaning: So what? What difference does it make?
It was pushed aside, removed from the מצוה

phrases.english: And when it became uncovered again, so what?
It was already pushed aside!
phrases.notes: He means: once the wind covered it, the blood was out of the מצוה of covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה מַאי הָוֵי? הָא אִידְּחִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the duty to cover returns when the blood becomes uncovered again.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wind's covering pushed the blood out of the מצוה, it should stay out even after it is uncovered again.

steps.title: A מצוה is not permanently pushed aside
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from רבי יוחנן's rule that there is no permanent pushing-aside with מצוות. The מצוה was only on hold while the blood was covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This teaches that there is no permanent pushing-aside when it comes to מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by drawing a general rule from רבי יוחנן's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוחנן obligates covering once the blood is exposed again, the wind's covering must not have cancelled the מצוה. It only made the מצוה impossible for a while. When the blood is uncovered, the duty is back.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches; we learn from here
A מצוה is not permanently cancelled just because it was temporarily impossible

steps.whatToRemember: אין דיחוי אצל מצות: if a מצוה becomes impossible for a while, it comes back when it becomes possible again. That is why wind-covered blood that is later exposed must be covered.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 15. When a person covered the blood himself, he already did the מצוה once (וכסהו), so he is exempt. When the wind covered it, he never did the מצוה, so it comes back.
steps.whyThisMatters: אין דיחוי אצל מצות is a general principle that the גמרא uses in other places about whether a temporary block ends a מצוה forever.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This teaches
there is no permanent pushing-aside when it comes to מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת אֵין דִּיחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about דיחוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a general principle out of the ruling itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the wind covered the blood, the מצוה was cancelled for good.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה is not permanently cancelled. It returns once it can be done again.

steps.title: Why is blood soaked into the ground still obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling that wind-covered blood which stayed covered is exempt, using a ברייתא that says blood soaked into the ground must still be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between this and what a ברייתא teaches: one who slaughters, and the blood soaked into the ground, must cover it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבי יוחנן. If blood soaked into the ground must still be covered, why is blood that the wind covered exempt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the blood is no longer out in the open, because the wind's dirt or the ground itself hides it. Yet the ברייתא still requires כיסוי. So it seems that being hidden by something other than the person should not exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (introduces a comparison that challenges a ruling)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: And what is different
from that which is taught in a ברייתא:
One who slaughters, and the blood was absorbed into the ground,
is obligated to cover it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the מצוה returns if the blood is uncovered again, the גמרא now attacks the other half of רבי יוחנן's ruling, that blood which stays covered is exempt.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that if the wind covered the blood and it stayed covered, one is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood absorbed into the ground is also hidden without the person doing anything, yet the ברייתא obligates covering it. So wind-covered blood should also be obligated.

steps.title: In the ברייתא the blood's mark can still be seen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about blood whose mark is still visible on the ground, so it is not really covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about when the mark of the blood is still recognizable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The blood in the ברייתא did not fully disappear, and you can still see its mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that left a visible mark is still considered uncovered, so the מצוה of כיסוי still applies. In רבי יוחנן's case, the wind truly covered the blood so nothing is seen. The two cases are different, and רבי יוחנן's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other case being compared)
A mark or impression left behind

steps.whatToRemember: Blood is exempt from כיסוי only when it is truly covered. If its mark can still be seen, even if it soaked into the ground, you must still cover it.

phrases.english: There, it is when its mark is recognizable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא of the ברייתא to a specific situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood absorbed into the ground counts as covered, so the ברייתא contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about blood whose mark is still visible, which counts as uncovered. Fully covered blood is exempt, as רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: New משנה: blood mixed with water, wine, or animal blood
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches when blood that got mixed with other liquids must still be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Blood that got mixed with water: if the mixture still looks like blood, one must cover it. If it got mixed with wine, we picture the wine as if it were water. If it got mixed with the blood of a בהמה...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It asks what happens when the blood that must be covered gets mixed into another liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With water, the test is simple: if the mix still looks like blood, you must cover it. With wine, you cannot use your eyes, so you imagine the wine as water and ask whether that mix would look like blood. The משנה then starts the case of mixing with the blood of a בהמה, whose blood does not need covering.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it as though (we imagine it as something else)
A domesticated animal (its blood does not need covering)

steps.confusionAlert: With wine, the משנה does not say to look at the actual mix. Because wine's color can hide the blood, you imagine the wine as water and judge it that way.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Blood that became mixed with water:
if it has the appearance of blood,
one is obligated to cover it.
If it became mixed with wine,
we view it as though it is water.
If it became mixed with the blood of a domesticated animal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous discussion is finished. This opens a new משנה on a new topic: blood mixed with other liquids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood mixed with water must be covered if the mix still looks like blood. If it is mixed with wine, we judge it as if the wine were water.
